title: Advisory soft-locks move out of channel_posts into channel_locks

story.as_a: session about to edit a file
story.i_want_to: keep channel_lock, channel_unlock and channel_locks working exactly as today while their rows live in a table of their own
story.so_that: channel_posts can become the message store, where every row is a message with one attachment

rationale: PRD section 4 (channel_lock row): a soft-lock is a coordination hint, not a message, and release 4 moves it out of channel_posts before that table becomes the message store (US-52.22). Today Coordination.lock_file/5 (lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:1057) writes a channel_posts row under the reserved claim: key with a clamped TTL of at most 3600 s, and lock special cases run through the whole message path: the reserved-prefix guard, the private TTL marker, the lock branch of ChannelPost.release_changeset/3, and the lock share cap in recent_page/3. channel_claims cannot hold locks instead: it is the exactly-once handoff claim with an open/done lifecycle a hint does not have, and release 7 deletes it. So locks get their own small table, and the message path loses every lock branch.

acceptance_criteria.description: A table channel_locks (tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, host, target, note, expires_at, timestamps), RLS enabled like channel_posts, schema Loopctl.Coordination.ChannelLock, with the unique index channel_locks_slot_uidx on (tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, target); tenant_id, project_id, agent_id and expires_at are set on the struct, never cast.

Coordination.lock_file/5 upserts the caller's channel_locks slot with expires_at = now + lock_ttl_seconds/1 (clamped to [60, 3600], default 900), through the same project_writable_by_agent/4 gate, secret denylist scan of note, session_id and host, and audit entry as today; it returns {:ok, lock, :created} or {:ok, lock, :updated} and writes no channel_posts row.

Coordination.unlock_file/5 deletes only the caller's own (agent_id, session_id, target) slot row and audits it under soft_lock_released; another agent's lock, another session's lock, a missing lock and a malformed target all return the byte-identical {:error, :not_found}.

Coordination.active_locks_page/3 reads live channel_locks rows (expires_at > now) newest first, keeps the page cap (default 100, clamp 200) and the per-agent fairness cap of 20 with its overflowed?/holders_truncated? flags, and POST/GET /api/v1/channel/locks and POST /api/v1/channel/locks/release answer with the same JSON fields as before this story.

The migration copies every live claim:-keyed channel_posts row (expires_at > now, quarantined_at IS NULL, expires_at <= updated_at + 3600 s) into channel_locks with ON CONFLICT on channel_locks_slot_uidx DO NOTHING, then deletes every claim:-keyed channel_posts row and drops channel_posts_soft_lock_idx; running the copy twice inserts nothing the second time.

No lock branch is left on the message path: reserved_key_prefix_check/1, the @soft_lock_ttl_attr marker and resolve_expires_at/1's lock route, apply_lock_share_cap/4, soft_lock_row?/1, the lock and lock_target fields of channel_recent rows, and ChannelPost's own_lease_seconds/2 lock branch are deleted, and channel_recent returns no lock rows.
Loopctl.Workers.ChannelPostSweeper deletes expired channel_locks rows (expires_at < now) in the same run as expired posts, bounded by the same batch size.

Projects.Merge.merge_into/4 moves a source project's channel_locks rows to the target, with channel_locks_slot_uidx in @unique_keys so a colliding slot is reported as a merge conflict, not a raised constraint error.

expected_results: first :created, second :updated, one channel_locks row with target lib/foo.ex and expires_at <= now + 3600 s; zero channel_posts rows

preconditions: as TC-52.21.1; a second agent with no assigned story in project

test_cases.name: unlock deletes only the caller's slot; every other case is the same not_found (DataCase)
preconditions: locks on lib/foo.ex by (agent, s1), (agent, s2) and (agent2, s1)
expected_results: first {:ok, _} and one soft_lock_released audit row; the other two {:error, :not_found}; the (agent, s2) and (agent2, s1) rows remain

expected_results: 23 rows (20 + 3), holders_truncated true, no expired row; the JSON rows carry the same keys as the pre-story response fixture

test_cases.name: migration moves live locks and drops dead ones (DataCase migration test)
preconditions: channel_posts rows: a live claim:lib/a.ex lock, an expired claim:lib/b.ex lock, a quarantined claim:lib/c.ex lock, a claim:lib/d.ex row with a 30-day expires_at, an ordinary keyless post
steps: run its copy step a second time
expected_results: channel_locks holds lib/a.ex only; channel_posts holds only the keyless post; the second copy inserts 0 rows

test_cases.name: the message path has no lock branch (unit + DataCase)
preconditions: a live lock taken with lock_file/5 and a keyless post on the same project
expected_results: one row (the post), with no :lock or :lock_target key

test_cases.name: the sweep reaps expired locks (DataCase, channel_post_sweeper_test.exs)
preconditions: one expired and one live channel_locks row

test_cases.name: merge moves locks and reports a slot collision (DataCase, merge test)
preconditions: source and target projects; a lock on lib/a.ex by (agent, s1) in each, and one on lib/b.ex in the source
expected_results: {:error, {:merge_conflicts, [conflict]}} naming channel_locks_slot_uidx; after deleting the target's lib/a.ex lock the merge moves both source locks

test_cases.name: tenant isolation: another tenant cannot read or release a lock (DataCase)
preconditions: tenant A holds a lock on lib/a.ex; tenant B with its own agent

technical_notes: Lock functions today: lock_file/5 lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:1057, unlock_file/5 :1143, active_locks/3 :1192, active_locks_page/3 :1227, live_locks_scope/3 :1263, lock_ttl_seconds/1 :1314, lock_key_prefix/0 :1328, max_lock_ttl_seconds/0 :1332, soft_lock_row?/1 :1356, normalize_lock_target/1 :1415, fetch_owned_lock/5 :1464, resolve_expires_at/1 :1486, reserved_key_prefix_check/1 :1507; constants @lock_key_prefix :92, @lock_key_like :102, @reserved_key_prefix_message :112, @min/@max/@default_lock_ttl_seconds :132-134, @soft_lock_ttl_attr :141, @soft_lock_release_action :149, @max_active_locks_limit and fairness @max_locks_per_holder :154-184, @max_recent_locks :194, apply_lock_share_cap/4 :3624.

ChannelPost lock remnants to delete: @soft_lock_key_prefix and @max_soft_lock_ttl_seconds lib/loopctl/coordination/channel_post.ex:143-144 and own_lease_seconds/2 :442-448 (release_changeset/3 then clamps to retention_days only).

Callers: LoopctlWeb.ChannelLockController (lib/loopctl_web/controllers/channel_lock_controller.ex:119 create, :146 release, :165 index; row rendering :195 and :261) keeps its routes (router.ex:336-340) and response keys; render lock rows from %ChannelLock{} instead of %ChannelPost{}.
The lock read stays tenant-scoped only and oracle-safe (docs/repo-coordination-bus.md section 3.6); the write gate is project_writable_by_agent/4 (coordination.ex:900).

Secret scanning: reuse Loopctl.Security.SecretDenylist.contains_secret?/1 over note, session_id and host, the same per-field bounds as ChannelPost (channel_post.ex:148-156, 731); no quarantine worker for locks: a lock lives at most 3600 s.

Sweep: lib/loopctl/workers/channel_post_sweeper.ex:176 sweep_batch/1; add a second bounded delete for channel_locks in the same perform/1 and keep its telemetry. Cron unchanged (lib/loopctl/oban_config.ex:566).
Merge: add channel_locks to @project_tables and channel_locks_slot_uidx (columns agent_id session_id target) to @unique_keys in lib/loopctl/projects/merge.ex:41-63.
Migration drops channel_posts_soft_lock_idx (priv/repo/migrations/20260722150000_add_channel_posts_soft_lock_idx.exs:30). Name it after git fetch origin (README Lanes rule 3).

Docs: rewrite the soft-lock paragraphs of docs/repo-coordination-bus.md sections 3.2 and 3.6 to name channel_locks; mcp-server tool descriptions channel_lock/channel_unlock/channel_locks (mcp-server/index.js:4268, :4298, :4335) stay true and change only where they name channel_posts.
CHANGELOG.md: channel_recent rows no longer carry lock and lock_target (a wire change for any reader of those fields); channel_locks is the lock read.
non_goals: Per-session lock isolation through holder identity: the slot stays (agent_id, session_id) as today; nothing in this release changes who may release a lock.
Removing the lock rate cap: US-52.26.

failure_modes.partition: n/a: every lock call is one statement or one transaction against loopctl's own Postgres inside the request; a client that lost the reply retries, and AC-52.21.2's slot upsert makes that retry a refresh.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.21.1 and AC-52.21.5: a lock lives only in channel_locks, and the migration carries every live lock across, so a deploy loses no live lock.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.21.2: a retried lock upserts the same slot; AC-52.21.5: a re-run copy inserts nothing twice.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.21.4: a session too slow to refresh its lock loses it to expires_at, which every read filters, so a stalled session never holds a file.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.21.7: expired rows are reaped by the existing ChannelPostSweeper Oban cron; everything else runs inline in the request process.

definition_of_done: On production after deploy: SELECT count(*) FROM channel_posts WHERE key LIKE 'claim:%' returns 0.
From an MCP session: channel_lock on lib/foo.ex, then channel_locks on the same project lists it with its target, then channel_unlock removes it.
defaults: Live lock rows only are migrated; expired, quarantined and over-ceiling claim: rows are dropped (owner may change).
